title: [WT-19] Integration and hardening: flip worktreeMode on, close parity, sweep file-only edges
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §7 (migration) and §8 (file-only dependency sweep). This is the epic's ONE integration-and-hardening task. The epic touched shared types (types/schema.ts: worktreeMode, workspaceMode, landingRetry), the MCP wire (claim/get_context workspace, finalize_attempt unlanded) and both wrappers, so full regression runs here.

Objective: turn worktree mode on by default only after the whole flow is proven end to end, and close the gaps no single slice could see.

Deliverable:
1. Flip the default in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts: `resolveWorktreeMode` returns 'on' when settings.worktreeMode is unset. Add vitest cases in validators.test.ts for unset→on, 'off'→off and 'on'→on. Change docs/CONFIGURATION.md's default to on, with the §7.4 rollback note ('off' restores shared mode).
2. Add the MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_ and MOE_BOARD_ families to the compared families in scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1.
3. File-only dependency sweep with moe.set_task_dependencies. Start from the governor audit list in §8: V07←01f37ac6, V04c←V08b, RF04←90664db1, RF07←465ee875, RF07←80930ce6, R13←R11e, R13←2cf1c6be, 724e31fa←e7f4026a, 01f37ac6←e7f4026a. For every still-open task's edge A←B, apply the §8 re-derivation rule: keep it if A names anything B produces; drop it only when the sole overlap is a shared existing file. The completion summary lists each edge as kept or dropped, with a reason.
4. Full regression (record pass counts):
   - npm test in packages/moe-daemon, packages/moe-proxy and packages/moe-claude-plugin;
   - bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and pwsh scripts/tests/postflight.ps1;
   - the worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} suites from WT-08T;
   - parity-check.{sh,ps1};
   - cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test, run under a jetbrains-gradle lease (moe.acquire_resource);
   - npm run lint.
5. End-to-end check in a throwaway repo made by `git init` under mktemp, with worktreeMode on. Two tasks in parallel touch disjoint files and both land on main. A third conflicts, goes to unlanded, then lands after the resume. Assert main's history is linear with no force-push (reflog shows only fast-forward updates).
6. Whole-epic adversarial pass (adversarial-self-review) over `git diff <epic base>..main` against the doc's §2-§6 contracts: drift between producer and consumer (daemon field names vs wrapper reads), sh/ps1 twin drift, codes documented in WT-17 but never emitted. Fix findings inside these files, or file them as bug: tasks in this epic.
7. Post the flip runbook (TROUBLESHOOTING section from WT-16) to #general for the human. Say that this project's worker seats stop with MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING until the control checkout is switched to moe/control.

NOT in scope: new features; re-editing docs other than CONFIGURATION.md (findings there become bug: tasks); changing shared-mode behavior.

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/validators.test.ts && npm test && cd ../.. && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh && npm run lint
definitionOfDone: resolveWorktreeMode defaults to 'on' (validators.test.ts covers unset/on/off) and docs/CONFIGURATION.md states default on plus the 'off' rollback.
parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 compare the MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_ and MOE_BOARD_ families, and both exit 0.
Every audited dependsOn edge, and every open edge re-derived by the §8 rule, is kept or dropped via moe.set_task_dependencies, with the list and reasons in the completion summary.
Full regression is green with recorded counts: daemon/proxy/claude-plugin npm test, postflight.{sh,ps1}, worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}, ./gradlew test (under the jetbrains-gradle lease) and npm run lint.
The throwaway-repo end-to-end run lands two parallel tasks plus one conflict-resumed task on main with fast-forward-only history.
The whole-epic adversarial findings are fixed or filed as bug: tasks, and the flip runbook is posted to #general naming MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.

implementationPlan.description:
Flip settings.worktreeMode's default to 'on' (DoD 1). Before editing, read WT-01's landed code (task-6cf120a38b344e72b7bab8b9faf806f1) and Serena decision-worktree-attempt-workspace-contract.

validators.ts:
- In resolveWorktreeMode, the ONE place the default lives, an undefined key now resolves to 'on'.
- 'off' still gives 'off' and 'on' still gives 'on'.
- Keep WT-01's refusal of every other stored value, null included (INVALID_INPUT).
- Update the function's doc comment. Also update ProjectSettings.worktreeMode's comment in types/schema.ts, but only if that comment states the default; that is a one-line edit, reported in modifiedFiles.

validators.test.ts:
- The absent case now expects 'on'.
- Keep explicit 'off' and 'on' cases, which gives DoD 1's unset/on/off coverage.

Tests that encode the old default:
- After the flip, a WORKING claim in any daemon test whose settings omit worktreeMode records workspaceMode 'worktree'.
- Run the full daemon suite. For each test whose INTENT is shared mode, pin `worktreeMode: 'off'` in that test's settings fixture instead of changing its assertions. Expected candidates: WT-01's shared claim cases, WT-02's shared branch-policy cases, and any claim fixture asserting workspace === projectPath.
- The exception is WT-01's own 'absent' case, which now asserts worktree mode.
- List every such file in complete_step.modifiedFiles and in the summary.

docs/CONFIGURATION.md:
- The worktreeMode row, written by WT-17, says the default is 'on'.
- Add the §7.4 rollback note:
  - Setting 'off' restores shared mode for NEW attempts. An open attempt keeps its pinned mode.
  - The control checkout goes back to a moe/work-<date> branch cut from main.
  - Rollback never moves main.

Error handling: an invalid stored value keeps failing loudly with INVALID_INPUT. It never silently reads as the new default.

Test: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/validators.test.ts`. On WSL, see step 5's environment notes.

Close parity (DoD 2, plus item 1 of WT-S comment-54c4e7a6).

parity-check.sh:
- Append 'MOE_WORKTREE_' 'MOE_LAND_' 'MOE_CONTROL_' 'MOE_BOARD_' 'MOE_PUSH_' 'MOE_MIGRATION_' to the section-1 family loop. That loop already fails when a family is empty in sh or differs between the twins.
- Add MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE to section 2's code list, the require_both list.
- Do NOT add MOE_WRAPPER_ as a family. At HEAD the sh wrapper carries eight internal MOE_WRAPPER_* names that the ps1 lacks: ARGV, CURRENT_HASH, DEFERRED_HASH, LAUNCH_HASH, PARSE_ERR, PARSE_RC, PATH and REFUSED_HASH.

parity-check.ps1:
- Add the same six families to $dynamicPatterns. The existing patterns use [A-Z_]+, so make the new ones accept digits if any landed code carries one; grep both wrappers to check.
- Add MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE to $required.

Stale allowlist:
- Both INTERNAL_PLUMBING lists name MOE_ATTR_UNDECLARED, MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDE, MOE_ATTR_POLICY_OVERRIDE and MOE_COMMIT_BOARD_STATE. No wrapper carries these any more: they were renamed to MOE_LAND_*, and WT-04 renamed those to MOE_PY_*.
- Remove the entries that neither wrapper contains, and keep the mechanism.
- Fix parity-check.ps1's NOTE comment: the names are now MOE_PY_*, and MOE_PY_ is not a compared family.

If a new family shows a token in only one twin:
- An internal env-bridge name joins the allowlist in BOTH scripts, with a comment.
- An operator-visible code missing from one twin is an epic defect. Emit it from the missing twin's equivalent site. If that is a one-line wrapper edit, make it and report it in modifiedFiles. If it is larger, file a bug: task and stop, because DoD 2 needs exit 0.

Error handling: both scripts must keep failing on any asymmetry and on an empty family. Never add a whole family to the allowlist.

Test: run `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$(wslpath -w scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1)"`. Both must exit 0.

Commit an end-to-end check of the whole flow (DoD 5) as a new file, scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs.

Model it on WT-04T's scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs (task-dd5daa4b789645d29b192176390884be):
- the same CLI shape, `<sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`;
- a `cli` fake-CLI mode;
- one result line per scenario, and exit 1 on any failure;
- no output line starting with SKIP.

Setup:
- The real wrappers with the shared fake daemon+proxy. Per WT-S comment-ce50a0ee, no real daemon is needed.
- One scratch repo from `git init` under mktemp, with branch main.
- The control checkout on moe/control.
- .moe/project.json settings {worktreeMode:'on'}, as the runbook leaves a project.

Scenarios:
(a) parallel. Launch two worker seats at once, with different worker ids and tasks (task-a, task-b). Each fake CLI writes its own file in its W (its cwd, per WT-05) and completes. Both must land:
- main gains exactly two commits;
- `git log --first-parent main` is linear;
- every `git reflog refs/heads/main` entry's new value descends from its old value (fast-forward only, never forced);
- neither W holds .moe.
(b) conflict-resume.
- task-c's fake CLI changes a line that task-a already landed differently.
- The landing ends unlanded on a conflict, main does not move, and the fake records finalize_attempt outcome 'unlanded'.
- A second session of task-c gets the LANDING-CONFLICT prompt (WT-11). Its fake CLI removes the markers and completes, and the task lands.
- History stays linear and fast-forward only.
(c) WT-S comment-54c4e7a6 item 2:
- The remote race: A publishes while B's fetch and push fail. There must be no fork (local == origin), and B ends unlanded 'remote'.
- An unknown push outcome that receipt_replay later resolves.
- If WT-08T/WT-09's held-out worktree-landing suites already cover these, name those cases here and let step 5 run them. Add a case to this file only if one is missing.

Fake-proxy support:
- Reuse the knobs WT-04T, WT-08T and WT-11 added: per-seat task ids, workspace, finalize 'unlanded', landingRetry.
- Add a missing knob to scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js only as an opt-in knob: with it unset, every answer stays byte-identical.
- Never edit a held-out suite.

Error handling: a scenario that can't be set up, for example because git is missing or a fixture command fails, fails with its reason. It never passes vacuously.

Test: `node scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(mktemp -d)" "$(command -v bash)"` prints ok for (a) and (b), and for (c) when its cases live here.

File-only dependency sweep (DoD 3, design §8), using moe.set_task_dependencies with removeDependsOn.

Candidates:
- The audit list: V07←01f37ac6, V04c←V08b, RF04←90664db1, RF07←465ee875, RF07←80930ce6, R13←R11e, R13←2cf1c6be, 724e31fa←e7f4026a, 01f37ac6←e7f4026a.
- Every dependsOn edge A←B of every task that is not DONE or ARCHIVED. Collect them with moe.list_tasks or moe.search_tasks.
- If either end of an edge is DONE or ARCHIVED, record the edge as 'moot'.

Rule (§8):
- Keep A←B when A's description, DoD or plan names anything B produces: a symbol, tool, setting, field, code, or a file B creates.
- Drop it only when the sole overlap is a shared existing file.

Safety: never put two shared-mode writers on one file. Dropping a file-only edge is safe only once this project actually runs in worktree mode. Before any drop, confirm one of these:
- the running daemon's get_context for a WORKING claim shows workspace.mode 'worktree';
- or project settings resolve to 'on' AND the control checkout's HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control.

The live daemon is the IDE-bundled build, so an older build shows no workspace at all, which counts as shared mode. While the project is still in shared mode, KEEP every file-only edge with the reason 'shared mode still live; drop after the §7.3 runbook', and carry that drop list into step 7's post for the governor.

Leave the WT chain's own edges alone.

Record every candidate as kept, dropped or moot, with its reason. That list goes verbatim into the complete_task summary.

Error handling: if a set_task_dependencies call is refused (a cycle, a missing id), record it with the error. Never retry it blindly.

Full regression, run once, fresh, after steps 1-4 (DoD 4; it also re-proves DoD 1, 2 and 5).

Canonical POSIX gate, from the repo root:
```
(cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/validators.test.ts && npm test) && (cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test) && (cd packages/moe-claude-plugin && npm test) && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && node scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(mktemp -d)" "$(command -v bash)" && npm run lint
```
Windows legs:
- `node.exe scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell`;
- parity-check.ps1 and worktree-landing.ps1 under Windows PowerShell 5.1;
- `cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"`, run while holding the jetbrains-gradle lease: moe.acquire_resource {resourceId:'jetbrains-gradle'}, released on every path (Serena convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease and gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl).

Environment notes (WSL):
- Run against a HEAD snapshot of the repo on /mnt/d, with this task's files copied over and cmp-checked, so peers' unlanded bytes can't leak in.
- Scrub MOE_* and CLAUDE* from the env of the bash legs, so the seat's own MOE_WORKER_ID and session id never reach the wrappers under test.
- The shared checkout's node_modules are Windows installs. For the three npm test legs, use a native Linux node_modules that matches HEAD's lockfiles (Serena gotcha-linux-vitest-reuse-native-node-modules), or run them under Windows node (pattern-qa-windows-native-vitest-from-wsl).
- Never run npm install or npm run build in the shared checkout.

Record pass counts for every leg (DoD 4), and say exactly how each leg ran. Each harness takes tens of minutes, so run them in the foreground, or poll a background run until it finishes.

Error handling:
- A failure in this task's files: fix it, then re-run the whole gate.
- A failure that also reproduces on a clean HEAD snapshot is pre-existing: report it with that evidence, and never weaken an assertion.
- A slice defect found here becomes a bug: task, filed in step 6.

Whole-epic adversarial review (DoD 6, first half). Load adversarial-self-review.

The diff: `git diff a1f971f5^..HEAD` (WT-S's first checkpoint is the epic base), limited to the epic's files:
- both wrappers;
- the daemon tools and state touched by WT-01, WT-02, WT-03, WT-03b (task-9eae3377dd504f8b8007986d51c651e9) and WT-16;
- WT-10P's proxy change;
- WT-15's JetBrains exclusion;
- the suites.

Check each item against the design doc's §1-§7:
1. Producer/consumer drift. Compare exactly what both wrappers read and send against what the daemon defines:
- the claim and get_context `workspace` {mode, path, branch, target};
- finalize_attempt 'unlanded' with unlandedReason, conflictPaths and rescueRef;
- Task.landingRetry {reason, paths, rescueRef, targetTip, count, at};
- the complete_task worktree branch policy.
2. sh/ps1 twin drift that parity-check's token families can't see: the same guard order, the same refusal routes, the same detail text.
3. Codes WT-17's docs document but the code never emits, and codes the code emits but nobody documents.
4. WT-S comment-54c4e7a6 item 3:
- In remote mode, no path moves the local target without remote confirmation (§2.3).
- No worktree materializes .moe: not W, not the gate worktree (WT-10G), not the hook worktree (§2.2 L7).
5. The epic rails:
- Rail 1: main moves only by a CAS after the gate, never by force.
- Rail 3: worktrees never hold .moe runtime.
- Rail 4: shared mode is unchanged when worktreeMode is 'off'.
6. WT-03b's two fixes are present: landingRetry is denylisted, and a release keeps a retrying row WORKING.

Error handling for findings:
- Fix a finding that sits inside this task's files.
- Anything else becomes a `bug:` task in this epic, filed via moe.create_task with a four-part description, a DoD and the evidence, and listed in the summary.

If this review changes any byte, re-run step 5's gate and submit that output to complete_task.

Post the flip runbook for the human (DoD 6, second half).

Send it to #general (chan-b6d8273b) with moe.chat_send, and check routingTargets. If they come back [], re-send the post to #governors.

The post must contain:
- A quote of, or a link to, WT-16's TROUBLESHOOTING runbook: §7.3 steps 1-6, including WT-10M's migration landing `--land-branch moe/work-2026-10-24`, and the §7.4 rollback.
- A plain warning about the flip. Once the daemon runs a build with it, every worker seat in this project whose claim says worktree mode stops with MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING and reports its task BLOCKED, until the control checkout is switched to moe/control. To avoid that, set worktreeMode 'off' explicitly before rebuilding the daemon or the IDE plugin, and remove it only at runbook step 6.
- Step 4's deferred drop list, for the governor to apply once the runbook is done.

Then call complete_task with step 5's gate evidence and a summary containing:
- the pass counts per leg;
- the sweep list;
- the ids of any bug tasks filed;
- the runbook message id.

In the summary, also test-check that every DoD item maps to its evidence.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Spike self-review notes for the planner:
(1) In the verification command, use `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash` (and `... powershell` on a Windows seat) in place of a bare `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`. That matches WT-04..WT-14 and gets the safe wrapper's timeout handling.
(2) Deliverable 5, the end-to-end run, needs no real daemon. scripts/tests/postflight.sh already ships a shared fake daemon+proxy (its claim/finalize knobs live at the handlers) and a fake CLI ($TMP_DIR/fake-cli). Drive three worker launches against one `git init` scratch repo through that harness, the way the WT-08T worktree-landing suites do.
(3) dependsOn was capped at 20, so task-5998f871 was dropped here. It is still covered transitively through WT-04 and WT-13.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Contract corrections from the WT-S revision after QA reject 1. Where this comment and the row's description differ, the revised docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md and this comment win. Section numbers are unchanged; rollback is still §7.4.
1. Parity-check: add the MOE_PUSH_ and MOE_MIGRATION_ families, plus the single code MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE, to the four families already listed.
2. The end-to-end check must include:
   - QA's two-seat publication race: A publishes while B's fetch and push fail. Expect no fork (local == origin) and B unlanded `remote`.
   - An unknown push outcome that receipt_replay then resolves.
3. The adversarial pass must confirm both of these:
   - in remote mode, no path moves the local target without remote confirmation (§2.3);
   - no worktree materializes `.moe/`: not W, not the gate worktree, not the hook worktree (rail 3).
4. The flip follows the corrected runbook: §7.3, with the migration landing and no human merge.

comments.author: architect-899a90d6
comments.content:
Two hardening items WT-03 (task-9a39bf6a) left out of its slice, for this task's adversarial pass:
1. The UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST in server/WebSocketServer.ts lacks 'landingRetry'. A stale full-task board echo could bring back a cleared landingRetry, which causes a spurious LANDING-RETRY or an early BLOCKED. A board client could also forge one.
2. nextStatusForRelease in state/workerLifecycle.ts routes a WORKING row whose steps are all COMPLETED to REVIEW. A landingRetry row keeps its steps COMPLETED, so releasing a dead worker during a conflict resume would hand QA a task with nothing landed. The row should stay WORKING while landingRetry is set.
Both are small. If WT-19 is over its file cap, split them into their own row.

comments.content:

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
End-to-end against a real built daemon: rejected. It needs Linux-native node_modules and dist builds of three packages in WSL, and WT-S (comment-ce50a0ee) recommends the shared fake daemon. Producer/consumer drift is covered by step 6's explicit contract cross-check instead.

Fixing WT-03's two landingRetry gaps in this row: rejected, because they need four more daemon files. They were split out as WT-03b (task-9eae3377), which WT-11 now waits on.

Dropping file-only edges unconditionally: rejected. While the project still runs in shared mode, that would put two writers on one file. Edges are deferred until the runbook has run.

Adding MOE_WRAPPER_ as a whole family: rejected, because eight sh-only internal names exist. Only the single MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE code is required in both wrappers.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Default:
- WT-01 keeps the worktreeMode default only in resolveWorktreeMode.
- Only WORKING claims get worktree mode.
- The attempt pins the mode, so the flip affects new attempts only.

Test fixtures:
- Daemon tests whose settings omit worktreeMode flip to worktree mode for WORKING claims.
- Pin 'off' where a test's intent is shared mode.

Dependencies:
- WT-19's dependsOn sits at the cap of 20.
- Every later row is still covered transitively: WT-19 → WT-17/WT-18 → WT-16 → WT-10M → WT-14 → … → WT-10G/WT-10P, WT-04T and WT-03b (via WT-11).

Live daemon:
- The running daemon is the IDE-bundled Windows build, so new fields show up only after a plugin rebuild.
planningNotes.risks:
The flip is product-wide:
- Once a daemon build carries it, any project left unconfigured gets worker seats that report their tasks BLOCKED with MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.
- The runbook post must lead with the 'set off before rebuilding' advice.

Other risks:
- Old-default tests may sit in several daemon test files. Pin 'off' in them; never weaken an assertion.
- The regression legs span WSL, Windows and Gradle under a lease, and take tens of minutes. Record how each leg ran.
- Slices may have drifted from the design. The adversarial pass compares landed code with landed code, not with this plan's assumptions.
